Quiver.arborescenceMk.code:
Quiver.arborescenceMk.{u, u_1} {V : Type u} [Quiver V] (r : V) (height : V → ℕ)
  (height_lt : ∀ ⦃a b : V⦄, (a ⟶ b) → height a < height b)
  (unique_arrow : ∀ ⦃a b c : V⦄ (e : a ⟶ c) (f : b ⟶ c), a = b ∧ HEq e f)
  (root_or_arrow : ∀ (b : V), b = r ∨ ∃ a, Nonempty (a ⟶ b)) : Arborescence V
Quiver.arborescenceMk.comment:
To show that `[Quiver V]` is an arborescence with root `r : V`, it suffices to
- provide a height function `V → ℕ` such that every arrow goes from a
  lower vertex to a higher vertex,
- show that every vertex has at most one arrow to it, and
- show that every vertex other than `r` has an arrow to it.

Quiver.arborescenceMk.fullDefinition: noncomputable def arborescenceMk {V : Type u} [Quiver V] (r : V) (height : V → ℕ)     (height_lt : ∀ ⦃a b⦄, (a ⟶ b) → height a < height b)     (unique_arrow : ∀ ⦃a b c : V⦄ (e : a ⟶ c) (f : b ⟶ c), a = b ∧ HEq e f)     (root_or_arrow : ∀ b, b = r ∨ ∃ a, Nonempty (a ⟶ b)) :     Arborescence V where   root := r   uniquePath b :=     ⟨Classical.inhabited_of_nonempty (by       rcases show ∃ n, height b < n from ⟨_, Nat.lt.base _⟩ with ⟨n, hn⟩       induction' n with n ih generalizing b       · exact False.elim (Nat.not_lt_zero _ hn)       rcases root_or_arrow b with (⟨⟨⟩⟩ | ⟨a, ⟨e⟩⟩)       · exact ⟨Path.nil⟩       · rcases ih a (lt_of_lt_of_le (height_lt e) (Nat.lt_succ_iff.mp hn)) with ⟨p⟩         exact ⟨p.cons e⟩), by       have height_le : ∀ {a b}, Path a b → height a ≤ height b := by         intro a b p         induction' p with b c _ e ih         · rfl         · exact le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt ih (height_lt e))       suffices ∀ p q : Path r b, p = q by         intro p         apply this       intro p q       induction' p with a c p e ih <;> cases' q with b _ q f       · rfl       · exact False.elim (lt_irrefl _ (lt_of_le_of_lt (height_le q) (height_lt f)))       · exact False.elim (lt_irrefl _ (lt_of_le_of_lt (height_le p) (height_lt e)))       · rcases unique_arrow e f with ⟨⟨⟩, ⟨⟩⟩         rw [ih]⟩
Quiver.arborescenceMk.description: The definition describes how to construct an arborescence structure given a root vertex, a height function that maintains a strict increasing order along arrows, and conditions ensuring uniqueness and connectivity of arrows to vertices from the root.

WideSubquiver.code: WideSubquiver.{v, u_1} (V : Type u_1) [Quiver V] : Type (max u_1 v)
WideSubquiver.comment:
A wide subquiver `H` of `G` picks out a set `H a b` of arrows from `a` to `b`
for every pair of vertices `a b`.

NB: this does not work for `Prop`-valued quivers. It requires `G : Quiver.{v+1} V`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

WideSubquiver.fullDefinition: def WideSubquiver (V) [Quiver.{v + 1} V] :=   ∀ a b : V, Set (a ⟶ b)
WideSubquiver.description: The definition describes a type of subquiver where for each pair of vertices, a set of arrows from one vertex to the other is specified.

wide_subquiver.description: The definition describes a type of subquiver where for each pair of vertices, a set of arrows from one vertex to the other is specified.

quiver.symmetrify.lift.fullDefinition: def lift [HasReverse V'] (φ : Prefunctor V V') :     Prefunctor (Symmetrify V) V' where   obj := φ.obj   map f := match f with   | Sum.inl g => φ.map g   | Sum.inr g => reverse (φ.map g)
quiver.symmetrify.lift.description: This definition describes a method to lift a prefunctor from a quiver with reversible arrows to another quiver derived from symmetrizing the original one.

Quiver.IsPreconnected.code: Quiver.IsPreconnected.{u, u_4} (V : Type u_4) [Quiver V] : Prop
Quiver.IsPreconnected.comment:
A quiver is preconnected iff there exists a path between any pair of
vertices.
Note that if `V` doesn't `HasReverse`, then the definition is stronger than
simply having a preconnected underlying `SimpleGraph`, since a path in one
direction doesn't induce one in the other.
Quiver.IsPreconnected.fullDefinition: def IsPreconnected (V) [Quiver.{u + 1} V] :=   ∀ X Y : V, Nonempty (Path X Y)
Quiver.IsPreconnected.description: This definition characterizes a quiver as preconnected if there is a path between every pair of its vertices.

Quiver.zigzagSetoid.code: Quiver.zigzagSetoid.{u, u_1} (V : Type u_1) [Quiver V] : Setoid V
Quiver.zigzagSetoid.comment:
Two vertices are related in the zigzag setoid if there is a
zigzag of arrows from one to the other.

explanatories.Quiver.Path.nil: The theorem states that a path exists from any vertex to itself, known as the trivial path.
explanatories.Quiver.Path.comp: The definition describes a method for combining two paths so that if there is a path from one vertex to a second and another path from that second vertex to a third, then there is a direct path from the first vertex to the third.

Quiver.zigzagSetoid.fullDefinition: def zigzagSetoid : Setoid V :=   ⟨fun a b ↦ Nonempty (@Path (Symmetrify V) _ a b), fun _ ↦ ⟨Path.nil⟩, fun ⟨p⟩ ↦     ⟨p.reverse⟩, fun ⟨p⟩ ⟨q⟩ ↦ ⟨p.comp q⟩⟩
Quiver.zigzagSetoid.description: The definition establishes a setoid structure on a quiver where vertices are considered equivalent if they can be connected by a sequence of alternating arrows.

Quiver.wideSubquiverSymmetrify.comment:
A wide subquiver `H` of `Symmetrify V` determines a wide subquiver of `V`, containing an
arrow `e` if either `e` or its reversal is in `H`.

explanatories.WideSubquiver: The definition describes a type of subquiver where for each pair of vertices, a set of arrows from one vertex to the other is specified.
explanatories.Sum.inl: The left injection function constructs a sum type from an element of the first type.
explanatories.Sum.inr: The right injection into the sum type combines an element from one type with the sum type, indicating it originates from the second type.

Quiver.wideSubquiverSymmetrify.fullDefinition: def wideSubquiverSymmetrify (H : WideSubquiver (Symmetrify V)) : WideSubquiver V :=   fun _ _ ↦ { e | H _ _ (Sum.inl e) ∨ H _ _ (Sum.inr e) }
Quiver.wideSubquiverSymmetrify.description: The definition describes a method to derive a wide subquiver from a symmetrified version of a quiver, ensuring that if an arrow or its reversal is present in the original wide subquiver, it will also belong to the derived subquiver.

Finset.memberFamily_induction_on.comment:
Induction principle for finset families. To prove a statement for every finset family,
it suffices to prove it for
* the empty finset family.
* the finset family which only contains the empty finset.
* `ℬ ∪ {s ∪ {a} | s ∈ 𝒞}` assuming the property for `ℬ` and `𝒞`, where `a` is an element of the
  ground type and `𝒜` and `ℬ` are families of finsets not containing `a`.
  Note that instead of giving `ℬ` and `𝒞`, the `subfamily` case gives you
  `𝒜 = ℬ ∪ {s ∪ {a} | s ∈ 𝒞}`, so that `ℬ = 𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily` and `𝒞 = 𝒜.memberSubfamily`.

This is a way of formalising induction on `n` where `𝒜` is a finset family on `n` elements.

See also `Finset.family_induction_on.`

Down.compression.fullDefinition: def compression (a : α) (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) : Finset (Finset α) :=   (𝒜.filter fun s => erase s a ∈ 𝒜).disjUnion       ((𝒜.image fun s => erase s a).filter fun s => s ∉ 𝒜) <|     disjoint_left.2 fun s h₁ h₂ => by       have := (mem_filter.1 h₂).2       exact this (mem_filter.1 h₁).1
Down.compression.description: The down-compression of a collection of finite sets involves removing a specified element from those sets that contain it, provided the resulting sets are not already included in the original collection.

UV.compress.code:
UV.compress.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra α] [DecidableRel Disjoint]
  [DecidableRel fun x x_1 => x ≤ x_1] (u v a : α) : α
UV.compress.comment:
UV-compressing `a` means removing `v` from it and adding `u` if `a` and `u` are disjoint and
`v ≤ a` (it replaces the `v` part of `a` by the `u` part). Else, UV-compressing `a` doesn't do
anything. This is most useful when `u` and `v` are disjoint finsets of the same size.

explanatories.Disjoint: A definition characterizing two elements of a lattice as disjoint if their greatest lower bound is the smallest element in that lattice.

UV.compress.fullDefinition: def compress (u v a : α) : α :=   if Disjoint u a ∧ v ≤ a then (a ⊔ u) \ v else a
UV.compress.description: UV-compressing an element modifies it by replacing a portion if certain conditions regarding disjointness and size are met, specifically substituting part of the element with another while leaving it unchanged otherwise.

reduce the cardinality, so we keep all elements whose compression is already present.

Finset.upShadow.code: Finset.upShadow.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α] [Fintype α] (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) : Finset (Finset α)
Finset.upShadow.comment:
The upper shadow of a set family `𝒜` is all sets we can get by adding one element to any set in
`𝒜`, and the (`k` times) iterated upper shadow (`upShadow^[k]`) is all sets we can get by adding
`k` elements from any set in `𝒜`.

explanatories.Finset.sup: This definition describes a function that computes the supremum of the images of elements from a finite set under a given function, using a specific order structure that includes a least element.
explanatories.Finset.image: This definition specifies a way to obtain the image of a finite set under a given function, producing a new finite set consisting of the outputs of the function applied to each element of the original set.
explanatories.Insert.insert: An operation is defined that allows an element to be added to a collection of another type.

Finset.upShadow.fullDefinition: def upShadow (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) : Finset (Finset α) :=   𝒜.sup fun s => sᶜ.image fun a => insert a s
Finset.upShadow.description: The upper shadow of a family of sets consists of all sets that can be formed by adding one element to any set within that family, and its iterated versions allow adding multiple elements.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.comment:
The relation we induct along in the proof by DeVos of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem.
`(s₁, t₁) < (s₂, t₂)` iff
* `|s₁ * t₁| < |s₂ * t₂|`
* or `|s₁ * t₁| = |s₂ * t₂|` and `|s₂| + |t₂| < |s₁| + |t₁|`
* or `|s₁ * t₁| = |s₂ * t₂|` and `|s₁| + |t₁| = |s₂| + |t₂|` and `|s₁| < |s₂|`.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.fullDefinition: private def DevosMulRel : Finset α × Finset α → Finset α × Finset α → Prop :=   Prod.Lex (· < ·) (Prod.Lex (· > ·) (· < ·)) on fun x ↦     ((x.1 * x.2).card, x.1.card + x.2.card, x.1.card)
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: The relation defined for pairs of finite sets compares their products based on size and certain tie-breaking criteria in order to facilitate a proof of the Cauchy-Davenport theorem.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code:
devosMulRel_iff.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Group α] [DecidableEq α] {x y : Finset α × Finset α} :
  DevosMulRel x y ↔
    (x.1 * x.2).card < (y.1 * y.2).card ∨
      (x.1 * x.2).card = (y.1 * y.2).card ∧ y.1.card + y.2.card < x.1.card + x.2.card ∨
        (x.1 * x.2).card = (y.1 * y.2).card ∧ x.1.card + x.2.card = y.1.card + y.2.card ∧ x.1.card < y.1.card

to standard `aesop`:

Finpartition.equitabilise_aux.code:
Finpartition.equitabilise_aux.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α] {s : Finset α} {m a b : ℕ} {P : Finpartition s}
  (hs : a * m + b * (m + 1) = s.card) :
  ∃ Q,
    (∀ x ∈ Q.parts, x.card = m ∨ x.card = m + 1) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ P.parts, (x \ (filter (fun y => y ⊆ x) Q.parts).biUnion id).card ≤ m) ∧
        (filter (fun i => i.card = m + 1) Q.parts).card = b
Finpartition.equitabilise_aux.comment:
Given a partition `P` of `s`, as well as a proof that `a * m + b * (m + 1) = s.card`, we can
find a new partition `Q` of `s` where each part has size `m` or `m + 1`, every part of `P` is the
union of parts of `Q` plus at most `m` extra elements, there are `b` parts of size `m + 1` and
(provided `m > 0`, because a partition does not have parts of size `0`) there are `a` parts of size
`m` and hence `a + b` parts in total.

  [DecidableRel G.Adj] (ε : 𝕜) (s t : Finset α) : Prop
SimpleGraph.IsUniform.comment:
A pair of finsets of vertices is `ε`-uniform (aka `ε`-regular) iff their edge density is close
to the density of any big enough pair of subsets. Intuitively, the edges between them are
random-like.

explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.

SimpleGraph.IsUniform.fullDefinition: def IsUniform (s t : Finset α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃s'⦄, s' ⊆ s → ∀ ⦃t'⦄, t' ⊆ t → (s.card : 𝕜) * ε ≤ s'.card →     (t.card : 𝕜) * ε ≤ t'.card → |(G.edgeDensity s' t' : 𝕜) - (G.edgeDensity s t : 𝕜)| < ε
SimpleGraph.IsUniform.description: A pair of vertex sets in a simple graph is defined as ε-uniform if their edge density is approximately similar to that of larger pairs of subsets, indicating a random-like edge distribution between them.

simple_graph.is_uniform.fullDefinition: def IsUniform (s t : Finset α) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃s'⦄, s' ⊆ s → ∀ ⦃t'⦄, t' ⊆ t → (s.card : 𝕜) * ε ≤ s'.card →     (t.card : 𝕜) * ε ≤ t'.card → |(G.edgeDensity s' t' : 𝕜) - (G.edgeDensity s t : 𝕜)| < ε

Finpartition.IsEquipartition.card_intere.code:
Finpartition.IsEquipartition.card_interedges_sparsePairs_le'.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2}
  [LinearOrderedField 𝕜] [DecidableEq α] {A : Finset α} {P : Finpartition A} {G : SimpleGraph α} [DecidableRel G.Adj]
  {ε : 𝕜} (hP : P.IsEquipartition) (hε : 0 ≤ ε) :
  ↑((P.sparsePairs G ε).biUnion fun x =>
          match x with
          | (U, V) => G.interedges U V).card ≤
    ε * (↑A.card + ↑P.parts.card) ^ 2

SimpleGraph.regularityReduced.fullDefinition: @[simps] def regularityReduced (ε δ : 𝕜) : SimpleGraph α where   Adj a b := G.Adj a b ∧     ∃ U ∈ P.parts, ∃ V ∈ P.parts, a ∈ U ∧ b ∈ V ∧ U ≠ V ∧ G.IsUniform ε U V ∧ δ ≤ G.edgeDensity U V   symm a b := by     rintro ⟨ab, U, UP, V, VP, xU, yV, UV, GUV, εUV⟩     refine ⟨G.symm ab, V, VP, U, UP, yV, xU, UV.symm, GUV.symm, ?_⟩     rwa [edgeDensity_comm]   loopless a h := G.loopless a h.1
SimpleGraph.regularityReduced.description: A graph is defined such that it retains edges between pairs of subsets from a given partition that are ε-uniform and meet a specified edge density threshold.

SimpleGraph.regularityReduced_adj.code:
SimpleGraph.regularityReduced_adj.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [LinearOrderedField 𝕜] [DecidableEq α]
  {A : Finset α} (P : Finpartition A) (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (ε δ : 𝕜) (a b : α) :
  (regularityReduced P G ε δ).Adj a b =
    (G.Adj a b ∧ ∃ U ∈ P.parts, ∃ V ∈ P.parts, a ∈ U ∧ b ∈ V ∧ U ≠ V ∧ G.IsUniform ε U V ∧ δ ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity U V))

  [Nonempty α] (hPα : P.parts.card * 16 ^ P.parts.card ≤ Fintype.card α) (hPε : 100 ≤ 4 ^ P.parts.card * ε ^ 5)
  (hε₁ : ε ≤ 1) {hU : U ∈ P.parts} {hV : V ∈ P.parts} {A B : Finset (Finset α)} (hA : A ⊆ (chunk hP G ε hU).parts)

SzemerediRegularity.increment.code:
SzemerediRegularity.increment.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] {P : Finpartition univ}
  (hP : P.IsEquipartition) (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (ε : ℝ) : Finpartition univ
SzemerediRegularity.increment.comment:
The **increment partition** in Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma.

If an equipartition is *not* uniform, then the increment partition is a (much bigger) equipartition
with a slightly higher energy. This is helpful since the energy is bounded by a constant (see
`Finpartition.energy_le_one`), so this process eventually terminates and yields a
not-too-big uniform equipartition.

SzemerediRegularity.le_sum_distinctPairs.code:
SzemerediRegularity.le_sum_distinctPairs_edgeDensity_sq.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
  {P : Finpartition univ} {hP : P.IsEquipartition} {G : SimpleGraph α} [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ} [Nonempty α]
  (x : { i // i ∈ P.parts.offDiag }) (hε₁ : ε ≤ 1) (hPα : P.parts.card * 16 ^ P.parts.card ≤ Fintype.card α)
  (hPε : 100 ≤ 4 ^ P.parts.card * ε ^ 5) :
  ↑(G.edgeDensity (↑x).1 (↑x).2) ^ 2 + ((if G.IsUniform ε (↑x).1 (↑x).2 then 0 else ε ^ 4 / 3) - ε ^ 5 / 25) ≤
    (∑ i ∈ SzemerediRegularity.distinctPairs hP G ε x, ↑(G.edgeDensity i.1 i.2) ^ 2) / 16 ^ P.parts.card

SimpleGraph.Subgraph.induce.code: SimpleGraph.Subgraph.induce.{u} {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} (G' : G.Subgraph) (s : Set V) : G.Subgraph
SimpleGraph.Subgraph.induce.comment:
The induced subgraph of a subgraph. The expectation is that `s ⊆ G'.verts` for the usual

  (hv : v = v') : G.Walk u' v'
SimpleGraph.Walk.copy.comment:
Change the endpoints of a walk using equalities. This is helpful for relaxing
definitional equality constraints and to be able to state otherwise difficult-to-state
lemmas. While this is a simple wrapper around `Eq.rec`, it gives a canonical way to write it.

The simp-normal form is for the `copy` to be pushed outward. That way calculations can
occur within the "copy context."
SimpleGraph.Walk.copy.fullDefinition: protected def copy {u v u' v'} (p : G.Walk u v) (hu : u = u') (hv : v = v') : G.Walk u' v' :=   hu ▸ hv ▸ p
SimpleGraph.Walk.copy.description: This definition provides a method to change the endpoints of a walk in a simple graph by leveraging equalities, allowing for flexibility in manipulating the endpoints while maintaining the walk's structure.

explanatories.SimpleGraph.symm: The theorem establishes that the adjacency relation in a simple graph is symmetric.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.Adj.symm: The theorem demonstrates that if one vertex is adjacent to another in a simple graph, then the second vertex is also adjacent to the first, confirming the symmetry of the adjacency relation.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.Dart.symm: This definition describes a method to obtain the dart that has the opposite orientation of a given dart in a simple graph.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.Reachable.symm: This theorem establishes that if one vertex is reachable from another in a simple graph, then the reverse is also true, indicating a symmetric relationship in reachability.
explanatories.Equiv.left_inv: This theorem asserts that the inverse function of an equivalence relation is a left inverse of the original function.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.Iso.symm: This definition specifies that the inverse of a graph isomorphism between two simple graphs exists and establishes an isomorphism back from the second graph to the first.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.iso_image: This theorem states that the image of a connected component under an isomorphism between two simple graphs is equal to a map of the connected component if and only if the connected component of a specific vertex in the first graph is the same as that component.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.ConnectedComponent.iso_inv_i: This theorem states that the invertibility of an isomorphism between two simple graphs ensures that the connected component of a vertex in the first graph corresponds to the image of that component under the relation of the second graph.
explanatories.Equiv.right_inv: This theorem states that the inverse function of an equivalence relation has a right inverse that retrieves the original function.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.Iso.connectedComponentEquiv: This definition states that an isomorphism between two graphs creates a one-to-one correspondence between their connected components.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.

explanatories.Subtype.ext_val: This theorem asserts that if two elements of a subtype are equal when viewed as their underlying values, then the elements themselves must also be equal.
explanatories.SimpleGraph.Subgraph.Adj.symm: This theorem establishes that if two vertices are adjacent in a subgraph, then they are also adjacent in the reverse order, confirming the symmetry of the adjacency relationship.
explanatories.Subtype.val: The value of a subtype is the underlying element from the base type that satisfies a given property.

  Finset (G.Walk u v)
SimpleGraph.finsetWalkLength.comment:
The `Finset` of length-`n` walks from `u` to `v`.
This is used to give `{p : G.walk u v | p.length = n}` a `Fintype` instance, and it
can also be useful as a recursive description of this set when `V` is finite.

See `SimpleGraph.coe_finsetWalkLength_eq` for the relationship between this `Finset` and
the set of length-`n` walks.

SimpleGraph.finsetWalkLength.fullDefinition: def finsetWalkLength (n : ℕ) (u v : V) : Finset (G.Walk u v) :=   match n with   | 0 =>     if h : u = v then by       subst u       exact {Walk.nil}     else ∅   | n + 1 =>     Finset.univ.biUnion fun (w : G.neighborSet u) =>       (finsetWalkLength n w v).map ⟨fun p => Walk.cons w.property p, fun _ _ => by simp⟩
SimpleGraph.finsetWalkLength.description: This definition specifies a finite set of walks of a specified length between two vertices in a simple graph.

simple_graph.finset_walk_length.code:
SimpleGraph.finsetWalkLength.{u} {V : Type u} (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableEq V] [G.LocallyFinite] (n : ℕ) (u v : V) :
  Finset (G.Walk u v)
simple_graph.finset_walk_length.comment:
The `Finset` of length-`n` walks from `u` to `v`.
This is used to give `{p : G.walk u v | p.length = n}` a `Fintype` instance, and it
can also be useful as a recursive description of this set when `V` is finite.

See `SimpleGraph.coe_finsetWalkLength_eq` for the relationship between this `Finset` and
the set of length-`n` walks.

SimpleGraph.«term_□_».comment:

SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian.comment:
An *Eulerian trail* (also known as an "Eulerian path") is a walk
`p` that visits every edge exactly once.  The lemma `SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian.IsTrail` shows
that these are trails.

Combine with `p.IsCircuit` to get an Eulerian circuit (also known as an "Eulerian cycle").

SimpleGraph.good_vertices_triangle_card.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ}
  {s t u : Finset α} [DecidableEq α] (dst : 2 * ε ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity s t)) (dsu : 2 * ε ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity s u))
  (dtu : 2 * ε ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity t u)) (utu : G.IsUniform ε t u) (x : α)
  (hx : x ∈ s \ (SimpleGraph.badVertices G ε s t ∪ SimpleGraph.badVertices G ε s u)) :
  ε ^ 3 * ↑t.card * ↑u.card ≤
    ↑(image (fun x_1 => (x, x_1))
          (filter
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (y, z) => G.Adj y z)
            (filter (G.Adj x) t ×ˢ filter (G.Adj x) u))).card

SimpleGraph.triangle_counting'.code:
SimpleGraph.triangle_counting'.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] {ε : ℝ} {s t u : Finset α}
  (dst : 2 * ε ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity s t)) (hst : G.IsUniform ε s t) (dsu : 2 * ε ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity s u))
  (usu : G.IsUniform ε s u) (dtu : 2 * ε ≤ ↑(G.edgeDensity t u)) (utu : G.IsUniform ε t u) :
  (1 - 2 * ε) * ε ^ 3 * ↑s.card * ↑t.card * ↑u.card ≤
    ↑(filter
          (fun x =>
            match x with
            | (a, b, c) => G.Adj a b ∧ G.Adj a c ∧ G.Adj b c)
          (s ×ˢ t ×ˢ u)).card
SimpleGraph.triangle_counting'.comment:
The **Triangle Counting Lemma**. If `G` is a graph and `s`, `t`, `u` are sets of vertices such
that each pair is `ε`-uniform and `2 * ε`-dense, then a proportion of at least
`(1 - 2 * ε) * ε ^ 3` of the triples `(a, b, c) ∈ s × t × u` are triangles.

  {t : Finset (α × β × γ)} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] ⦃x y z : α ⊕ β ⊕ γ⦄ :
  (graph t).Adj x y →
    (graph t).Adj x z →
      (graph t).Adj y z →
        ∃ a b c,
          {in₀ a, in₁ b, in₂ c} = {x, y, z} ∧

SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.card_neighborFinse.code:
SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.card_neighborFinset_union_of_not_adj.{u} {V : Type u} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
  {G : SimpleGraph V} [DecidableRel G.Adj] {n k ℓ μ : ℕ} {v w : V} (h : G.IsSRGWith n k ℓ μ) (hne : v ≠ w)
  (ha : ¬G.Adj v w) : (G.neighborFinset v ∪ G.neighborFinset w).card = 2 * k - μ
SimpleGraph.IsSRGWith.card_neighborFinse.comment:
Assuming `G` is strongly regular, `2*(k + 1) - m` in `G` is the number of vertices that are
adjacent to either `v` or `w` when `¬G.Adj v w`. So it's the cardinality of
`G.neighborSet v ∪ G.neighborSet w`.

SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.code: SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.{u_1} {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M : G.Subgraph) : Prop
SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.comment:
The subgraph `M` of `G` is a matching if every vertex of `M` is incident to exactly one edge in `M`.
We say that the vertices in `M.support` are *matched* or *saturated*.

Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exis.code:
Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective.{u, v} {ι : Type u} {α : Type v} [DecidableEq α]
  (t : ι → Finset α) :
  (∀ (s : Finset ι), s.card ≤ (s.biUnion t).card) ↔ ∃ f, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ (x : ι), f x ∈ t x
Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exis.comment:
This is the version of **Hall's Marriage Theorem** in terms of indexed
families of finite sets `t : ι → Finset α`.  It states that there is a
set of distinct representatives if and only if every union of `k` of the
sets has at least `k` elements.

Recall that `s.biUnion t` is the union of all the sets `t i` for `i ∈ s`.

This theorem is bootstrapped from `Finset.all_card_le_biUnion_card_iff_exists_injective'`,
which has the additional constraint that `ι` is a `Fintype`.

Fintype.all_card_le_rel_image_card_iff_e.code:
Fintype.all_card_le_rel_image_card_iff_exists_injective.{u, v} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq β]
  (r : α → β → Prop) [(a : α) → Fintype ↑(Rel.image r {a})] :
  (∀ (A : Finset α), A.card ≤ Fintype.card ↑(Rel.image r ↑A)) ↔ ∃ f, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ (x : α), r x (f x)
Fintype.all_card_le_rel_image_card_iff_e.comment:
This is a version of **Hall's Marriage Theorem** in terms of a relation
between types `α` and `β` such that `α` is finite and the image of
each `x : α` is finite (it suffices for `β` to be finite; see
`Fintype.all_card_le_filter_rel_iff_exists_injective`).  There is
a transversal of the relation (an injective function `α → β` whose graph is
a subrelation of the relation) iff every subset of
`k` terms of `α` is related to at least `k` terms of `β`.

Note: if `[Fintype β]`, then there exist instances for `[∀ (a : α), Fintype (Rel.image r {a})]`.

SemistandardYoungTableau.highestWeight.fullDefinition: def highestWeight (μ : YoungDiagram) : SemistandardYoungTableau μ where   entry i j := if (i, j) ∈ μ then i else 0   row_weak' hj hcell := by     simp only     rw [if_pos hcell, if_pos (μ.up_left_mem (by rfl) (le_of_lt hj) hcell)]   col_strict' hi hcell := by     simp only     rwa [if_pos hcell, if_pos (μ.up_left_mem (le_of_lt hi) (by rfl) hcell)]   zeros' not_cell := if_neg not_cell
SemistandardYoungTableau.highestWeight.description: This definition specifies the semistandard Young tableau of a given shape where each row contains the value corresponding to its row index, representing the highest weight configuration.

Finset.mulSpan.comment:
The span of a finset `s` is the finset of elements of the form `∏ a in s, a ^ ε a` where
`ε ∈ {-1, 0, 1} ^ s`.

This is an analog of the linear span in a vector space, but with the "scalars" restricted to
`0` and `±1`.

explanatories.Fintype.piFinset: This definition asserts that given a finset associated with each element of a type, one can construct a finset of all functions whose values correspond to those sets for each element.
explanatories.Finset.image: This definition specifies a way to obtain the image of a finite set under a given function, producing a new finite set consisting of the outputs of the function applied to each element of the original set.

Finset.mulSpan.fullDefinition: def mulSpan (s : Finset α) : Finset α :=   (Fintype.piFinset fun _a ↦ ({-1, 0, 1} : Finset ℤ)).image fun ε ↦ ∏ a in s, a ^ ε a
Finset.mulSpan.description: The span of a finite set consists of all possible products formed by taking elements from the set raised to the powers of either -1, 0, or 1, analogous to the linear span in a vector space but restricted to these specific scalars.

rothNumberNat.comment:
The Roth number of a natural `N` is the largest integer `m` for which there is a subset of
`range N` of size `m` with no arithmetic progression of length 3.
Trivially, `rothNumberNat N ≤ N`, but Roth's theorem (proved in 1953) shows that
`rothNumberNat N = o(N)` and the construction by Behrend gives a lower bound of the form
`N * exp(-C sqrt(log(N))) ≤ rothNumberNat N`.
A significant refinement of Roth's theorem by Bloom and Sisask announced in 2020 gives
`rothNumberNat N = O(N / (log N)^(1+c))` for an absolute constant `c`.

explanatories.ThreeAPFree.mono: If a larger set is 3GP-free, then any subset of it is also 3GP-free.
explanatories.Set.InjOn.mono: The theorem establishes that if a function is injective on a larger set, it remains injective when restricted to a smaller subset that is contained within the larger set.
explanatories.ThreeGPFree.mono: If a larger set is 3GP-free, then any subset of it is also 3GP-free.
explanatories.addRothNumber: The multiplicative Roth number of a finite set is defined as the size of its largest subset that is free of any three elements that can form a non-trivial geometric progression.
explanatories.Set.MapsTo.mono: The theorem states that if a function maps a subset to another set and if two subsets are related by inclusion, along with their images also being related by inclusion, then the function maps the smaller subset to the larger image set.
explanatories.Set.SurjOn.mono: The theorem demonstrates that if a function is surjective from a larger subset to a larger codomain, then it is also surjective from a smaller subset to a smaller codomain, provided that these subsets are appropriately ordered.
explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.
explanatories.OrderHom.mono: This theorem states that any order homomorphism between preordered types is monotonic, meaning it preserves the order between the input and output elements.

explanatories.Finset.range_mono: This theorem asserts that the range of a monotonic function is also a monotonic function.

Behrend.map.comment: The map that appears in Behrend's bound on Roth numbers.

explanatories.Pi.zero_apply: This theorem asserts that for any element of a collection where each element is an instance of the "zero" type, the application of the "zero" value to that element yields the "zero" value.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.zero_mul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, demonstrating that zero acts as a left absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.Finset.sum_const_zero: The sum of zero over any finite set equals zero.
explanatories.Pi.add_apply: This theorem examines the behavior of function composition involving a constant function that returns the "one" value.
explanatories.add_mul: This theorem defines the right distributive property of multiplication over addition in a specific algebraic structure.
explanatories.Finset.sum_add_distrib: The theorem demonstrates that the sum of values obtained by adding two functions over a finite set equals the sum of the values from each function computed separately over the same set.

Behrend.map.fullDefinition: def map (d : ℕ) : (Fin n → ℕ) →+ ℕ where   toFun a := ∑ i, a i * d ^ (i : ℕ)   map_zero' := by simp_rw [Pi.zero_apply, zero_mul, sum_const_zero]   map_add' a b := by simp_rw [Pi.add_apply, add_mul, sum_add_distrib]
Behrend.map.description: The defined map transforms functions from a finite set of size n to natural numbers into a single natural number, as utilized in Behrend's analysis of Roth numbers.

Finset.mulEnergy.code: Finset.mulEnergy.{u_1} {α : Type u_1} [DecidableEq α] [Mul α] (s t : Finset α) : ℕ
Finset.mulEnergy.comment:
The multiplicative energy `Eₘ[s, t]` of two finsets `s` and `t` in a group is the number of
quadruples `(a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂) ∈ s × s × t × t` such that `a₁ * b₁ = a₂ * b₂`.

The notation `Eₘ[s, t]` is available in scope `Combinatorics.Additive`.

product of the two sets.

explanatories.Nat.succ: This states the successor function for natural numbers, which yields the next integer by adding one to a given natural number.
explanatories.Fin.last: The largest element in a finite set defined by one more than a given natural number is identified.
explanatories.Finset.mem_univ: This theorem asserts that every element of a finitely enumerable type is a member of the universal finite set that contains all elements of that type.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Fin.ext_iff: Two finite numbers are equal if and only if their corresponding natural number representations are equal.
explanatories.Composition.boundaries: This definition describes a finite set of indices representing the leftmost points of all blocks in a composition, including an additional virtual point at the end for a corresponding equivalence with another representation of the composition.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.zero_le: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, any element is greater than or equal to zero.
explanatories.Nat.succ_pred_eq_of_pos: If a natural number is positive, then the predecessor of that number, when increased by one, equals the original number.
explanatories.Fin.succ: The successor of a finite number is produced by increasing its upper limit, resulting in a new finite number that is one greater.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.Fin.is_lt: A finite number is always less than its upper limit represented as a natural number.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Disjoint.symm: If two elements in a lattice are disjoint, then the second element is also disjoint from the first, establishing the symmetry of disjointness.
explanatories.Composition.ext_iff: This theorem establishes a relation between the equality of two compositions and the equality of their respective block structures.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.add_lt_add_left: This theorem establishes that if one element is strictly less than another, then adding a common element to both sides of the inequality preserves that strict relationship.
explanatories.LT.lt.trans_le: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second and that second element is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Nat.succ_eq_add_one: The successor of a natural number is equal to that number plus one.
explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.Nat.sub_le: The difference between two natural numbers is less than or equal to the first number.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.
explanatories.CompositionAsSet: This definition provides a set of boundaries for a given composition represented as a collection of consecutive integers from zero to one less than the specified natural number.
explanatories.Set.toFinset: This definition establishes a method for converting a set into a finite set representation, provided that the set has a finite type instance.
explanatories.Set.toFinset_setOf: This theorem establishes that the finite set of elements satisfying a predicate is equal to the finite set of those elements filtered from the universal finite set.
explanatories.forall_true_left: This theorem states that for any property dependent on a true proposition, it is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for the specific instance of true.
explanatories.Finset.mem_filter: This theorem states that an element belongs to the filtered version of a set if and only if it is in the original set and satisfies the filtering condition.
explanatories.true_and: The theorem demonstrates that the conjunction of a true proposition and any other proposition is equivalent to the other proposition itself.
explanatories.exists_prop: The existence of an element satisfying one proposition implies both that proposition and another proposition are true.
explanatories.Classical.or_iff_not_imp_left: The statement asserts that the disjunction of two propositions is equivalent to the implication that if the first is false, then the second must be true.
explanatories.Fin.val_zero: The value of the zero element in a finite structure is equal to the natural number zero.
explanatories.Fin.val_last: The value of the maximum finite number in a range is equal to the natural number representing the upper bound of that range.
explanatories.pos_iff_ne_zero: This theorem establishes that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, an element is positive if and only if it is not equal to zero.
explanatories.Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq: A natural number is less than the successor of another number if and only if it is either less than that number or equal to it.
explanatories.or_false: The theorem states that the disjunction of any proposition with a false proposition is equivalent to the original proposition itself.
explanatories.Nat.pred_lt_pred: If a natural number is not zero and is less than another natural number, then its predecessor is also less than the predecessor of the second number.
explanatories.ge_iff_le: The relation of one element being greater than or equal to another is equivalent to the latter being less than or equal to the former.
explanatories.ne_of_lt: This theorem claims that if one element is less than another in a preorder, then the two elements cannot be equal.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.add_eq_zero_iff: This theorem states that in a canonically ordered additive commutative monoid, the sum of two elements equals zero if and only if both elements are individually zero.
explanatories.and_false: The theorem establishes that the conjunction of any proposition with a false proposition is equivalent to false.
explanatories.add_left_inj: The equality of sums with a fixed element on the right side implies the equality of the other two elements in a right-cancelable additive structure.
explanatories.false_or: The theorem states that the disjunction of false with any proposition is equivalent to that proposition itself.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.false_or_iff: Theorem stating that a disjunction of a falsehood with a proposition is equivalent to the original proposition itself.
explanatories.add_right_inj: The equality of sums with a fixed element on the left side implies the equality of the other two elements in a left-cancelable additive structure.
explanatories.one_ne_zero: This theorem demonstrates that one is not equal to zero in any type that supports both one and zero.
explanatories.false_and_iff: Theorem stating that a conjunction of a falsehood with a proposition is equivalent to falsehood itself.
explanatories.Fin.val_mk: The value of a finite number constructed from a smaller natural number is equal to that natural number itself.
explanatories.Or.inr: If there is a proof of a proposition, it can be included in a disjunction as the second option.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.CompositionAsSet.boundaries: This definition provides a set of boundaries for a given composition represented as a collection of consecutive integers from zero to one less than the specified natural number.
explanatories.CompositionAsSet.zero_mem: This theorem asserts that zero is an element of the boundaries of a given composition represented as a set.
explanatories.Fin.zero_le: Any finite number is greater than or equal to zero.
explanatories.CompositionAsSet.getLast_mem: This theorem asserts that the last element of a composition is included in its boundaries.
explanatories.Subtype.ext_iff: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if and only if their corresponding values in the underlying set are equal.

compositionAsSetEquiv.fullDefinition: def compositionAsSetEquiv (n : ℕ) : CompositionAsSet n ≃ Finset (Fin (n - 1)) where   toFun c :=     { i : Fin (n - 1) |         (⟨1 + (i : ℕ), by               apply (add_lt_add_left i.is_lt 1).trans_le               rw [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, add_comm]               exact add_le_add (Nat.sub_le n 1) (le_refl 1)⟩ :             Fin n.succ) ∈           c.boundaries }.toFinset   invFun s :=     { boundaries :=         { i : Fin n.succ |             i = 0 ∨ i = Fin.last n ∨ ∃ (j : Fin (n - 1)) (_hj : j ∈ s), (i : ℕ) = j + 1 }.toFinset       zero_mem := by simp       getLast_mem := by simp }   left_inv := by     intro c     ext i     simp only [add_comm, Set.toFinset_setOf, Finset.mem_univ,      forall_true_left, Finset.mem_filter, true_and, exists_prop]     constructor     · rintro (rfl | rfl | ⟨j, hj1, hj2⟩)       · exact c.zero_mem       · exact c.getLast_mem       · convert hj1     · simp only [or_iff_not_imp_left]       intro i_mem i_ne_zero i_ne_last       simp? [Fin.ext_iff] at i_ne_zero i_ne_last says         simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Fin.ext_iff, Fin.val_zero, Fin.val_last]           at i_ne_zero i_ne_last       have A : (1 + (i - 1) : ℕ) = (i : ℕ) := by         rw [add_comm]         exact Nat.succ_pred_eq_of_pos (pos_iff_ne_zero.mpr i_ne_zero)       refine ⟨⟨i - 1, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩       · have : (i : ℕ) < n + 1 := i.2         simp? [Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq, i_ne_last] at this says           simp only [Nat.succ_eq_add_one, Nat.lt_succ_iff_lt_or_eq, i_ne_last, or_false] at this         exact Nat.pred_lt_pred i_ne_zero this       · convert i_mem         simp only [ge_iff_le]         rwa [add_comm]       · simp only [ge_iff_le]         symm         rwa [add_comm]   right_inv := by     intro s     ext i     have : 1 + (i : ℕ) ≠ n := by       apply ne_of_lt       convert add_lt_add_left i.is_lt 1       rw [add_comm]       apply (Nat.succ_pred_eq_of_pos _).symm       exact (zero_le i.val).trans_lt (i.2.trans_le (Nat.sub_le n 1))     simp only [add_comm, Fin.ext_iff, Fin.val_zero, Fin.val_last, exists_prop, Set.toFinset_setOf,       Finset.mem_univ, forall_true_left, Finset.mem_filter, add_eq_zero_iff, and_false,       add_left_inj, false_or, true_and]     erw [Set.mem_setOf_eq]     simp [this, false_or_iff, add_right_inj, add_eq_zero_iff, one_ne_zero, false_and_iff,       Fin.val_mk]     constructor     · intro h       cases' h with n h       · rw [add_comm] at this         contradiction       · cases' h with w h; cases' h with h₁ h₂         rw [← Fin.ext_iff] at h₂         rwa [h₂]     · intro h       apply Or.inr       use i, h

Finset.exists_lt_sum_fiber_of_maps_to_of_nsmul_lt_sum.{u, v, w} {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {M : Type w} [DecidableEq β]
  {s : Finset α} {t : Finset β} {f : α → β} {w : α → M} {b : M} [LinearOrderedCancelAddCommMonoid M]
  (hf : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ∈ t) (hb : t.card • b < ∑ x ∈ s, w x) : ∃ y ∈ t, b < ∑ x ∈ filter (fun x => f x = y) s, w x
Finset.exists_lt_sum_fiber_of_maps_to_of.comment:
The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, strict inequality version:
if the total weight of a finite set of pigeons is greater than `n • b`, and they are sorted into
`n` pigeonholes, then for some pigeonhole, the total weight of the pigeons in this pigeonhole is
greater than `b`.

The pigeonhole principle for finitely many pigeons counted by weight, strict inequality version:

derangements.atMostOneFixedPointEquivSum.fullDefinition: def atMostOneFixedPointEquivSum_derangements [DecidableEq α] (a : α) :     { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f ⊆ {a} } ≃ Sum (derangements ({a}ᶜ : Set α)) (derangements α) :=   calc     { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f ⊆ {a} } ≃         Sum { f : { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f ⊆ {a} } // a ∈ fixedPoints f }           { f : { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f ⊆ {a} } // a ∉ fixedPoints f } :=       (Equiv.sumCompl _).symm     _ ≃ Sum { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f ⊆ {a} ∧ a ∈ fixedPoints f }           { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f ⊆ {a} ∧ a ∉ fixedPoints f } := by       -- Porting note: `subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter` no longer works with placeholder `_`s.       refine Equiv.sumCongr ?_ ?_       · exact subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter           (fun x : Perm α => fixedPoints x ⊆ {a})           (a ∈ fixedPoints ·)       · exact subtypeSubtypeEquivSubtypeInter           (fun x : Perm α => fixedPoints x ⊆ {a})           (¬a ∈ fixedPoints ·)     _ ≃ Sum { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f = {a} } { f : Perm α // fixedPoints f = ∅ } := by       refine Equiv.sumCongr (subtypeEquivRight fun f => ?_) (subtypeEquivRight fun f => ?_)       · rw [Set.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem, and_comm]         rfl       · rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_not_mem]         exact ⟨fun h x hx => h.2 (h.1 hx ▸ hx), fun h => ⟨fun x hx => (h _ hx).elim, h _⟩⟩     _ ≃ Sum (derangements ({a}ᶜ : Set α)) (derangements α) := by       -- Porting note: was `subtypeEquiv _` but now needs the placeholder to be provided explicitly       refine         Equiv.sumCongr ((derangements.subtypeEquiv (· ∈ ({a}ᶜ : Set α))).trans <|             subtypeEquivRight fun x => ?_).symm           (subtypeEquivRight fun f => mem_derangements_iff_fixedPoints_eq_empty.symm)       rw [eq_comm, Set.ext_iff]       simp_rw [Set.mem_compl_iff, Classical.not_not]
derangements.atMostOneFixedPointEquivSum.description: The collection of permutations that fix either a specific element or none at all is equivalent to the sum of the derangements on the set without that element and the derangements on the entire set.

FractionalOperation.IsValid.code: FractionalOperation.IsValid.{u_1} {D : Type u_1} {m : ℕ} (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : Prop
FractionalOperation.IsValid.comment: Fractional operation is valid iff nonempty.
FractionalOperation.IsValid.fullDefinition: def FractionalOperation.IsValid (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : Prop :=   ω ≠ ∅
FractionalOperation.IsValid.description: This defines a condition for a fractional operation to be considered valid, specifically that it must be nonempty.

FractionalOperation.tt.code:
FractionalOperation.tt.{u_1, u_3} {D : Type u_1} {m : ℕ} {ι : Type u_3} (ω : FractionalOperation D m)
  (x : Fin m → ι → D) : Multiset (ι → D)
FractionalOperation.tt.comment: Fractional operation applied to a transposed table of values.

explanatories.Multiset: The definition describes a multiset as a type representing finite collections of elements that allows for duplicates, formed by considering lists up to their permutations.
explanatories.Multiset.map: This definition outlines a way to create a new multiset by applying a function to each element of an existing multiset, preserving the count of each element according to how many times the function produces the same output.
explanatories.Function.swap: This definition indicates the absence of any specified content or structure within the provided context.

FractionalOperation.tt.fullDefinition: def FractionalOperation.tt {ι : Type*} (ω : FractionalOperation D m) (x : Fin m → ι → D) :     Multiset (ι → D) :=   ω.map (fun (g : (Fin m → D) → D) (i : ι) => g ((Function.swap x) i))
FractionalOperation.tt.description: This defines the application of a fractional operation to a transposed table of values, resulting in a multiset of mappings from a given index type to a specified type.

FractionalOperation.size.code: FractionalOperation.size.{u_1} {D : Type u_1} {m : ℕ} (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : ℕ
FractionalOperation.size.comment: Arity of the "output" of the fractional operation.
FractionalOperation.size.fullDefinition: def FractionalOperation.size (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : ℕ :=   Multiset.card.toFun ω
FractionalOperation.size.description: This defines a function that determines the arity, or size, of the output associated with a given fractional operation.

Function.AdmitsFractional.code:
Function.AdmitsFractional.{u_1, u_2} {D : Type u_1} {C : Type u_2} [OrderedAddCommMonoid C] {m n : ℕ}
  (f : (Fin n → D) → C) (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : Prop
Function.AdmitsFractional.comment: Cost function admits given fractional operation, i.e., `ω` improves `f` in the `≤` sense.

explanatories.ValuedCSP.Term.f: This specifies a function that provides the corresponding cost value from a valued combinatorial satisfaction problem based on a given input from its domain.
explanatories.Multiset.map: This definition outlines a way to create a new multiset by applying a function to each element of an existing multiset, preserving the count of each element according to how many times the function produces the same output.
explanatories.Multiset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of elements in a multiset based on a commutative additive monoid structure.
explanatories.FractionalOperation: This defines a fractional operation as a collection of finite mappings from a specific power of a given type to itself, allowing for multiple occurrences of each mapping.
explanatories.FractionalOperation.tt: This defines the application of a fractional operation to a transposed table of values, resulting in a multiset of mappings from a given index type to a specified type.
explanatories.FractionalOperation.size: This defines a function that determines the arity, or size, of the output associated with a given fractional operation.
explanatories.Finset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of a function's values at each element of a finite set.

Function.AdmitsFractional.fullDefinition: def Function.AdmitsFractional {n : ℕ} (f : (Fin n → D) → C) (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : Prop :=   ∀ x : (Fin m → (Fin n → D)),     m • ((ω.tt x).map f).sum ≤ ω.size • Finset.univ.sum (fun i => f (x i))
Function.AdmitsFractional.description: This defines a condition that states a cost function is enhanced by a specific fractional operation, meaning the operation provides a cost that is less than or equal to the original function's cost.

FractionalOperation.IsFractionalPolymorp.code:
FractionalOperation.IsFractionalPolymorphismFor.{u_1, u_2} {D : Type u_1} {C : Type u_2} [OrderedAddCommMonoid C]
  {m : ℕ} (ω : FractionalOperation D m) (Γ : ValuedCSP D C) : Prop
FractionalOperation.IsFractionalPolymorp.comment: Fractional operation is a fractional polymorphism for given VCSP template.

explanatories.ValuedCSP: This defines a template for a valued combinatorial satisfaction problem involving a specific domain and costs, accommodating various numeric and logical types.
explanatories.ValuedCSP.Term.f: This specifies a function that provides the corresponding cost value from a valued combinatorial satisfaction problem based on a given input from its domain.
explanatories.Function.AdmitsFractional: This defines a condition that states a cost function is enhanced by a specific fractional operation, meaning the operation provides a cost that is less than or equal to the original function's cost.

FractionalOperation.IsFractionalPolymorp.fullDefinition: def FractionalOperation.IsFractionalPolymorphismFor     (ω : FractionalOperation D m) (Γ : ValuedCSP D C) : Prop :=   ∀ f ∈ Γ, f.snd.AdmitsFractional ω
FractionalOperation.IsFractionalPolymorp.description: This defines a condition under which a fractional operation qualifies as a fractional polymorphism for a specified valued combinatorial satisfaction problem template.

FractionalOperation.IsSymmetric.code: FractionalOperation.IsSymmetric.{u_1} {D : Type u_1} {m : ℕ} (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : Prop
FractionalOperation.IsSymmetric.fullDefinition: def FractionalOperation.IsSymmetric (ω : FractionalOperation D m) : Prop :=   ∀ x y : (Fin m → D), List.Perm (List.ofFn x) (List.ofFn y) → ∀ g ∈ ω, g x = g y
FractionalOperation.IsSymmetric.description: This states the condition for a fractional operation to be symmetric.

FractionalOperation.tt.eq_1.code:
FractionalOperation.tt.eq_1.{u_1, u_3} {D : Type u_1} {m : ℕ} {ι : Type u_3} (ω : FractionalOperation D m)
  (x : Fin m → ι → D) : ω.tt x = Multiset.map (fun g i => g (swap x i)) ω

FractionalOperation.tt.eq_1.description: This theorem establishes an equality between the application of a fractional operation on a transposed table of values and the multiset of outputs obtained by mapping a function over the original fractional operation.

Ultrafilter.mul.code: Ultrafilter.mul.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} [Mul M] : Mul (Ultrafilter M)
Ultrafilter.mul.comment: Multiplication of ultrafilters given by `∀ᶠ m in U*V, p m ↔ ∀ᶠ m in U, ∀ᶠ m' in V, p (m*m')`.

explanatories.Ultrafilter.mul: The definition establishes a multiplication operation for ultrafilters that reflects the behavior of products in a multiplicative structure, ensuring convergence based on the filters' limiting properties.
explanatories.Ultrafilter.coe_inj: Two ultrafilters are equal if and only if their representations as filters are equal.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Filter.ext': A theorem stating that two filters are equal if they satisfy the same property for every predicate in terms of their convergence.
explanatories.Ultrafilter.eventually_mul: The theorem states that a property holds for the product of two ultrafilters if and only if it holds for the individual ultrafilters when considering the multiplication of their elements.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.

Ultrafilter.semigroup.fullDefinition: def Ultrafilter.semigroup {M} [Semigroup M] : Semigroup (Ultrafilter M) :=   { Ultrafilter.mul with     mul_assoc := fun U V W =>       Ultrafilter.coe_inj.mp <|         -- porting note (#11083): `simp` was slow to typecheck, replaced by `simp_rw`         Filter.ext' fun p => by simp_rw [Ultrafilter.eventually_mul, mul_assoc] }
Ultrafilter.semigroup.description: The definition establishes a semigroup structure for ultrafilters based on the semigroup structure of the underlying set.

(f l))       obtain ⟨p, hl₁⟩ := Fintype.card_pos_iff.mp ((congr_arg _ Nat.card_eq_fintype_card).mp (h₂ l₁))       by_cases hl₂ : p ∈ l₂       · exact ⟨p, hl₁, hl₂⟩       have key' : Fintype.card { q : q₂)).2)).resolve_right             fun h => (congr_arg (¬p ∈ ·) h).mp hl₂ (mkLine_ax (this q₁)).1)       have key' := ((Fintype.bijective_iff_injective_and_card f).mpr ⟨hf, key'⟩).2       obtain ⟨q, explanatories.Configuration.HasLines.mkLine: The definition establishes a way to create a line associated with two distinct points based on their membership in an existing line structure.
explanatories.Configuration.HasLines.mkLine_ax: The theorem states that for two distinct points associated with a given line structure, both points lie on the line created by those points.

Configuration.ProjectivePlane.mkLine_ax.description: The theorem establishes that in a projective plane, if two distinct points are taken, both points belong to the line created by those points.

Configuration.ProjectivePlane.card_point.code:
Configuration.ProjectivePlane.card_points.{u_1, u_2} (P : Type u_1) (L : Type u_2) [Membership P L]
  [ProjectivePlane P L] [Fintype P] [Finite L] : Fintype.card P = order P L ^ 2 + order P L + 1

explanatories.Fintype.card: This definition establishes that for a type that has a finite enumeration, the cardinality or number of elements in that type is a natural number.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.Nat.card: This definition assigns a natural number representing the cardinality of a type, with the convention that infinite types are assigned the value zero.
explanatories.Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order: The definition establishes the order of a projective plane as one less than the number of lines through a point or the number of points on a line.
explanatories.Configuration.ProjectivePlane.Dual.order: The theorem states that in a finite projective plane, the order of the dual configuration of lines equals the order of the original configuration of points and lines.

Configuration.ProjectivePlane.card_point.description: The theorem establishes that in a finite projective plane, the total number of points is equal to the square of the order of the plane plus the order of the plane plus one.
